newsitem.title: USA: U.S. watchdog wants sea turtle off menu.
newsitem.headline: U.S. watchdog wants sea turtle off menu.

text.p: A Florida environmental group wants the popular cookbook "Joy of Cooking" to remove suggestions for cooking and eating endangered sea turtles.
Sue Ellen Smith of the Sea Turtle Survival League said on Tuesday the group had written to the book's publisher Penguin Books USA requesting the references be deleted.
"I am discouraged to find that despite our education efforts 'Joy of Cooking' is encouraging its readers to cook and eat endangered sea turtles," the letter said.
"We believe Penguin books should be sensitive to this issue and realize its responsibilty by removing all references to cooking sea turtles found in 'Joy of Cooking'," it said.
It noted that killing sea turtles, listed as an endangered species, was illegal in the United States and punishable by a jail sentence.

Under the heading "Turtles and Terrapins," the book tells readers that because "handling and cooking these monsters" is difficult, "most of us are content to enjoy their highly prized, highly priced gelatinous meat reday-diced and in cans."
Smith told Reuters that Penguin had so far failed to reply to the letter. Penguin representatives were unavailable for comment.
